summary: Lane B (N11 / G53 / G54). No true broadcast deviation exists anywhere in rows 70-110: every stored date in the span is the real TV-Tokyo Saturday-09:30 first-run date of the title stored beside it, confirmed line by line against ja-WP 各話リスト, en-WP's three season lists and syobocal's per-airing records for ChID 7. What is wrong is the NUMBERING: our rows are animefillerlist's rows keyed by AFL's printed number, and AFL prints no 73 and prints 96 twice, so our rows 74-95 hold true episodes 73-94, our DB has no row 73, and true ep 95 ('Rima, Yaya, and the Pearls that Bind Them!', 2009-08-08) was lost when the two AFL rows numbered 96 collapsed — 126 rows for a 127-episode show. AFL's list order is additionally transposed at three adjacent pairs inside that span (its 75/76, 83/84, 90/91), which is why exactly those three of our rows carry their own true number and why the census flags an airdate_regression at each; the honest fix is the renumber (sort rows 74-95 by their correct stored date and assign 73-94), not 23 date repairs. Rows 107/108 are a DIFFERENT defect: correctly-numbered Party rows that hold each other's episode, repaired here as a title+date swap. Three genuine date defects sit outside the Doki span and are repaired: rows 35 (Sun), 37 (Tue) and 46 (Thu) carry AFL typos for what are plain Saturdays with no preemption in those weeks.

WHAT THE STATUS COLUMN MEANS. OK = number and date both true. NUM = the row's TITLE and DATE are a correct, real episode; only the NUMBER it sits under is wrong (no air_date repair is possible or wanted here — N11, Sean: no G54 ack for a numbering bug). SWAP = rows 107/108 hold each other's episode (a pure AFL transposition inside correctly-numbered Party rows) — repaired here as title+date.

THE DEFECT (N11). Our episode rows ARE animefillerlist's rows keyed by AFL's printed number. AFL's 127-row list prints no number 73 and prints 96 twice ('Rima, Yaya, and the Pearls that Bind Them!' then 'Unheard Pleas, Shattered Feelings.'), so: (a) our rows 74-95 hold true episodes 73-94 — one HIGHER than the truth; (b) our DB has no row 73 and only 126 rows, because the two AFL rows numbered 96 collapsed to one and true ep 95 ('Rima, Yaya, and the Pearls that Bind Them!' / りまとやや、真珠の絆！, 2009-08-08, AFL type manga_canon) was LOST; (c) our row 96 onwards is back in true numbering. AFL's list ORDER is also transposed at three adjacent pairs inside the span — its 75/76, 83/84 and 90/91 hold (true 75, true 74), (true 83, true 82), (true 90, true 89) — which is why those three of our rows carry their own true number while their neighbours are +1, and why the census sees an airdate_regression at each.

THE FIX, STATED AS AN OUTCOME (per row, not as a formula). Rows 74-95 must be renumbered to the true numbers in the table above; the simplest exact recipe is: take our rows 74-95, sort by their STORED air_date (every one is correct), and assign 73, 74, ... 94 in that order. That single operation absorbs both the +1 offset and the three transposed pairs. Number 95 then falls free and is exactly where the missing true ep 95 (2009-08-08) is inserted; rows 96-127 keep their numbers, with 107/108's contents swapped by the repairs in this verdict.

WHY A MONOTONE SOURCE_NUMBERING_SHIFTS ENTRY IS NOT ENOUGH (worth Sean's eye before apply). The Shift shape is drop[] + shifts[{from,offset}] — a monotone step function on the SOURCE number. {drop: [], shifts: [{from: 74, offset: -1}, {from: 97, offset: +1}]} would fix 18 of the 22 rows but (i) leaves the three transposed pairs swapped against broadcast (74=Utau's visit / 3-21 before 75=White Day / 3-14 — the regression survives, only renumbered), and (ii) maps BOTH AFL rows numbered 96 onto 95, so the second still overwrites the first and number 96 is left empty. The AFL→ours map that is actually true is: 74->73, 75->75, 76->74, 77->76, 78->77, 79->78, 80->79, 81->80, 82->81, 83->83, 84->82, 85->84, 86->85, 87->86, 88->87, 89->88, 90->90, 91->89, 92->91, 93->92, 94->93, 95->94, 96(first row printed)->95, 96(second)->96, 97-106 identity, 107->108, 108->107, 109-127 identity. Expressing it needs either a per-number map (with the duplicate disambiguated by AFL's LIST POSITION, not its printed number) or a G53 title+date block over 73-96.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE STORED G53 MAP (must move with the rows). AIR_DATE_OVERRIDES['shugo-chara'] is keyed by our CURRENT numbers and is applied AFTER translation in filterEpisodeRows, so a renumber silently re-points it. Re-key: 88->87, 92->91, 93->92, 94->93, 95->94; 23, 26, 96, 97, 98, 99, 100 unchanged; add 35 = 2008-06-07, 37 = 2008-06-21, 46 = 2008-08-23 (this verdict), and 95 = 2009-08-08 for the inserted row. Left un-re-keyed, the override that reads '92: 2009-07-11' would stamp 7-11 onto Beat Jumper (true 92, 7-18).

CONSEQUENCE FOR ANCHORS AND ANNOTATIONS (they travel with the row). Anchored rows in the span become: our 75 stays 75 (ch 29), 76->74 (ch 28), 77->76 (ch 29-30), 78->77 (ch 30), 80->79 (ch 30-31), 81->80 (ch 31-32). That REMOVES the ep-75/76 non-monotonicity: in true numbering 74 = White Day = ch 28 comes before 75 = Utau's visit = ch 29. The stored 'rearranged {28-28 after 29}' annotation on ep 76 and the A18 'reorder regime, rows 73-96' ruling are, for this pair, artifacts of the AFL numbering bug rather than an anime reorder — see flags. Also moving: the graft annotation on our 93 -> 92, and the divergence block eps 87-96 -> 86-96 (with the inserted true 95 to be typed).

ROW COUNT. 126 stored rows vs total_episodes 127; the renumber + the one insert makes 127. No other row in 70-110 has a wrong date: every stored date in the span is the true first-run TV Tokyo date of the title it sits with.

flags_for_sean: NUMBERING (N11) — the ask's core answer, stated per row in structure.notes. Our rows 74-95 hold TRUE episodes 73-94; rows 75, 83 and 90 are the three that coincidentally hold their own true number (AFL's list transposes its 75/76, 83/84, 90/91); row 96 onwards is already true. Nothing in 74-95 is an air_date defect — every stored date is the correct date for the title stored with it, so the correct instrument is the renumber, exactly as ruled (no G54 ack for a numbering bug). Recipe that is provably exact: sort our rows 74-95 by stored air_date and assign 73..94 in that order.

A MONOTONE SHIFT CANNOT EXPRESS THIS DEFECT. SOURCE_NUMBERING_SHIFTS is drop[] + shifts[{from,offset}], a monotone step function on the source number: {shifts:[{from:74,offset:-1},{from:97,offset:+1}]} fixes 18 of 22 rows but leaves the three transposed pairs reversed against broadcast AND maps both AFL rows numbered 96 onto our 95 (the second overwrites the first; number 96 ends up empty). Either the shape needs a per-number map with the duplicate disambiguated by AFL's LIST POSITION, or the span is pinned as a G53 title+date block over 73-96. Sean's call — I have given the exact target for every row either way.

MISSING EPISODE. True ep 95 'Rima, Yaya, and the Pearls that Bind Them!' (りまとやや、真珠の絆！), aired 2009-08-08 (ja-WP 第95話 / en-WP Doki row 44 / syobocal TID 1510 Count 95), has NO row in our DB — 126 rows for 127 episodes. It exists on AFL as the FIRST of the two rows printed '96' (typed manga_canon there, with AFL's 2010 year slip on the date). After the renumber, number 95 is free and this row belongs there. Its typing is not mine to rule: it sits inside the batch-17 'Lulu ?-egg arc' block (our rows 87-96 = true 86-96) that AFL calls canon and fandom records no chapter counterpart for, so it most likely joins that divergence annotation.

THE G53 MAP MUST BE RE-KEYED IF THE RENUMBER LANDS. AIR_DATE_OVERRIDES['shugo-chara'] is applied AFTER numbering translation in filterEpisodeRows, so the batch-19 keys point at the wrong rows the moment the span moves: 88->87, 92->91, 93->92, 94->93, 95->94 (23, 26, 96-100 unchanged). Un-re-keyed, '92: 2009-07-11' would stamp 7-11 onto Beat Jumper (true 92, 7-18) — a new defect created by the fix.

ANCHOR / ANNOTATION CONSEQUENCE (not a repair I am making, but it should be decided in the same sitting). After the renumber the anchored rows in the span become 75 (unchanged, ch 29), 76->74 (ch 28), 77->76, 78->77, 80->79, 81->80, and the ep-75/76 NON-MONOTONICITY DISAPPEARS: true 74 = White Day = ch 28 precedes true 75 = Utau's visit = ch 29. The stored annotation 'eps 76 rearranged {28-28 after 29}' and the A18 ruling 'reorder regime ... rows 73-96 ... adjacent anchors legitimately step backwards' are, for this pair, artifacts of AFL's numbering, not of the anime. Recommend re-deriving both after the renumber. The graft annotation on our 93 moves to 92; the divergence block 87-96 becomes 86-96.

GATE MISMATCH: batch20/validate-airdates.ts (copied from batch 19) rejects any repair whose field is not 'air_date', but this task's lane-B ask explicitly allows 'title' repairs and the 107/108 transposition cannot be honestly expressed without them (EPISODE_TITLE_OVERRIDES exists for exactly this — 'a transposition carries the title with the date'). Four of my seven repairs are the 107/108 pair (two title, two air_date). The gate needs the title field allowed, or those two rows need to travel as a structure finding.

NO G54 ACK ANYWHERE IN THIS SERIES. All four regression pairs have prosaic causes: 75/76, 83/84 and 90/91 are the AFL numbering/order defect (fix = renumber), 107/108 is an AFL transposition (fix = the four repairs here). Shugo Chara! never moved off Saturday 09:30 テレビ東京 in 127 episodes — syobocal's ChID-7 first-run sequence is unbroken week by week apart from the three New Year skips already carried correctly in our data (2007-12-22 -> 2008-01-05, 2008-12-27 -> 2009-01-10, 2009-12-26 -> 2010-01-09). order_only is therefore empty in this verdict, superseding the batch-19 verdict's provisional listing of the eight rows.
